Getting started with perglm

Source: vignettes/getting-started.Rmd
getting-started.Rmd

Fit the null model and test an exposure

perglm_test() tests an exposure contribution to a conditional mean using a GLM score calibrated by marginal exposure permutations. Supply the response and nuisance covariates in the formula, and supply the exposure separately.

Generate a small example with two nuisance covariates, a binary exposure, and a count outcome:

set.seed(42)
dat <- data.frame(z1 = rnorm(120), z2 = rnorm(120),
                  x = rbinom(120, 1, 0.3))
dat$y <- rpois(120, exp(0.3 + 0.2 * dat$z1 - 0.1 * dat$z2 + 0.2 * dat$x))

For a Poisson model with a log link, the working alternative adds an exposure coefficient to the linear predictor. The null hypothesis sets that coefficient to zero. The null formula y ~ z1 + z2 therefore excludes x and includes the usual implicit intercept.

set.seed(2026)
result <- perglm_test(
  y ~ z1 + z2,
  data = dat,
  exposure = dat$x,
  family = poisson(),
  B = 999L
)
result
#> 
#>  Permutation-calibrated GLM score test (poisson, log link)
#> 
#> data:  dat$x with null model y ~ z1 + z2
#> T = 1.6236, B = 999, p-value = 0.103
#> alternative hypothesis: true exposure coefficient is not equal to 0
result$p.value
#> [1] 0.103

The result is a standard R htest object. This example does not reject the null at the 5% level. No exposure coefficient estimate or confidence interval is calculated.

exposure uses ordinary R evaluation: dat$x supplies the vector explicitly. Binary and continuous numeric exposures are supported. Values must follow the same row order as data; names, when present, must match the model row names.

Read the result

The default alternative is "two.sided". The alternatives "greater" and "less" refer to the exposure coefficient on the link scale. With the log link above, a positive coefficient increases the conditional mean. With a decreasing link, a positive coefficient lowers the conditional mean.

result$statistic
#>        T 
#> 1.623595
c(nobs = result$nobs, B = result$B, exceedances = result$exceedances)
#>        nobs           B exceedances 
#>         120         999         102
result$null_diagnostics
#> $converged
#> [1] TRUE
#> 
#> $iterations
#> [1] 5
#> 
#> $max_score_correlation
#> [1] 1.242781e-13
#> 
#> $separation_checked
#> [1] FALSE
#> 
#> $gaussian_residual_check
#> NULL

The diagnostics describe null fitting and numerical checks; they do not verify the statistical assumptions. Conditional-mean validity requires a correct null mean model and the regularity conditions in the paper. The working outcome variance may be misspecified. This procedure does not test every possible form of conditional dependence.

Choose the permutation budget

The p-value is (1 + exceedances) / (B + 1), using inclusive tail comparisons. With B = 999L, the smallest attainable p-value is 0.001. Larger budgets give finer resolution and require more computation. The null model is fitted once; each shuffle recomputes exposure residuals and their empirical score variance.

Call set.seed() before testing to reproduce the permutation draws. The first seed above generates the example data; the second controls calibration. batch_size limits how many permutations are scored together and controls working memory. For successful runs, changing batching or retention settings preserves the result and final RNG state when the seed is unchanged.

Set keep_statistics = TRUE to retain the sampled scores in result$permuted_statistics. By default, that field is NULL.

Supported models and guarded failures

Working families include Gaussian, Bernoulli (binomial), Poisson, Gamma, inverse Gaussian, and negative binomial. Use family = "negative.binomial" to estimate a log-link model’s size, or a MASS::negative.binomial() family object to specify a fixed size. Fixed offsets can appear in the null formula.

Model observations must be complete, with unit prior weights and a full-rank nuisance design containing an intercept. Bernoulli outcomes must be coded zero or one; grouped binomial responses are unsupported. The model must have positive residual degrees of freedom and the exposure must retain variation after nuisance adjustment.

The function stops without a p-value for unsupported fits, including Bernoulli separation and Gaussian residuals indistinguishable from fitting roundoff. Undefined observed or permuted scores also stop calibration; draws are never discarded or redrawn. Inspect the data and null model before continuing.

Reference

Ai, J. and Niu, Z. (2026). Conditional independence testing through marginal permutation. arXiv:2611.03255.
